Runway introduces Praxis-1 to turn video learning into robot actions

The model is being tested with robotics partners, with a public open-weight release planned in the coming months.

The Robot Report ↗2 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Video knowledge becomes robot control

Runway’s Praxis-1 builds on large-scale video pretraining to select actions for physical robots. The premise is that general footage can teach object behavior and motion before adaptation to a particular task and body. This could reduce dependence on costly demonstrations collected directly with robot hardware.

Testing across different bodies

Early partners Noble Machines, Standard Bots and Ultra are testing the model on their own hardware. The examples cover two-arm manipulation, robot arms and mobile platforms, including interactions with cans and kitchen objects. These demonstrations do not establish that the policy can handle every task or unfamiliar environment.

Public weights are still planned

Access currently targets selected pre-launch partners, with a public open-weight release planned in the coming months. A cited 0.95 correlation comes from related world-model policy evaluation comparing simulated and physical results; it is not a 95% task-success rate for Praxis-1. Task-specific evidence and release conditions remain important before adoption.
